candidates: When adding non-obvious filtering or defensive logic that compensates for stale persisted state (e.g., entries in `shortcutKeys` that came from localStorage but were never registered in the current session), include an inline comment explaining *why* the filtering is required—not just what it does.

Keep PRs strictly scoped to their stated objective. If a diff contains changes that are unrelated to the PR title and description (e.g., new builder-detection mappings in a UI bug-fix PR), flag them and request extraction into a separate PR with its own description, tests, and documentation.

When calling functions such as `findLeafEntry` that search for a descendant and may legitimately return `null`/`undefined` (e.g., when all children are filtered out of the visible hash), always capture the return value in a variable and guard with a truthiness check before passing it to consumers like `gotoStory`; silently no-op when nothing is found rather than risking a runtime error.

Add JSDoc to every exported utility function in framework and shared packages (e.g., under `code/frameworks/`), documenting the function's purpose, each parameter, and the full range of return values—including graceful-failure paths (e.g., 'returns `false` when the version string cannot be coerced by semver').

In Vitest test files, place mock setup (`vi.mocked(...)`, `vi.spyOn(...)`) and default mock implementations in `beforeEach` blocks rather than inline within individual `it` blocks. Call `vi.clearAllMocks()` in a `beforeEach` or `afterEach` to prevent cross-test state leakage.
Proofread the prose in `docs/versions/` release-note JSON entries for grammar errors (e.g., possessive 'its' vs. contraction 'it's') before committing.

When updating MIGRATION.md with TypeScript configuration guidance, accurately state which `moduleResolution` modes (e.g., `bundler`, `nodenext`) reject extensionless imports (TS2691) and specify the exact setting required to keep them working (e.g., `allowImportingTsExtensions`). Do not imply extensionless imports 'continue to work' without qualifying which tsconfig resolver supports them, as this will regress users who followed earlier guidance in the same document.
